g.text: PRIME BRICK TOWER π(x) vs Li(x)

g.data-pedagogical: Riemann Explicit Error Bound: When every zero sits on σ = 0.5, |π(x) − Li(x)| is bounded by O(√x · ln x). Off-line zeros inflate the error exponent to O(x^max(σ, 1−σ))!
Prime Counting Staircase π(x): Each column adds 1 indivisible prime brick. Keeping zeta zeros on σ = 0.5 locks the staircase tightly to Li(x)!

path.data-pedagogical: Logarithmic Integral Li(x): The smooth curve predicting how many prime bricks appear up to x.

g.data-pedagogical: Zeta Drift Oscilloscope: Plots |σ - 0.5| over time. Flat at 0 means every prime harmonic is locked!

g.aria-label: Snap spinning brick to the 0.5 Critical Line
g.data-pedagogical: Snap Button: Resets σ directly to 0.5 and locks the prime brick staircase into harmonic rhythm.
